issues.description: The patch deletes the existing public `RcuOption::new_none` constructor even though the const/tracked-variable fix only required moving its inner implementation outside the verified block.
issues.rationale: `RcuOption::new_none` is an established public executable API and is semantically appropriate for the nullable wrapper. The patch successfully keeps `RcuInner::new_none` and `RcuOption::new(None)` working after moving the const implementation out of `#[verus_verify]`, so deleting the convenience constructor is not required by the tracked-variable fix. The collaborator explicitly asks why original code was deleted, and the thread remains unresolved on the merged final head. This violates `preserve-exec-code`: proof migration should retain existing executable APIs unless a concrete incompatibility requires their removal.
issues.verification: source-only; historical Verus not executed. Compared the fixed base and merged head, inspected the surviving nullable constructors, and read the complete archived and live remote discussion.
